body.purpose: Transcript line text, colored per source pen.

label.purpose: Title-block and rail field labels, tab names, pen state text; uppercase + tracking substitutes for the direction contract's condensed face.

mono.purpose: Timestamps, pen names, chart-speed readout, engine log.

motion.name: mark-lands
motion.purpose: New transcript line arriving on the chart; the system's one authored line-arrival motion.

components.name: Record Button
components.description: Primary Start recording action with a drawn pen-nib icon.
components.css: .ds-btn-record { display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 0.5rem; border: 1px solid #16233a; border-radius: 3px; background: #16233a; color: #e9f0ea; padding: 0.7rem 1rem; font-size: 0.8125rem; font-weight: 700; letter-spacing: 0.06em; cursor: pointer; box-shadow: 0 5px 14px -8px rgba(23,35,27,0.22); transition: transform 140ms cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1), box-shadow 140ms ease-out; } .ds-btn-record:hover { transform: translateY(-1px); box-shadow: 0 8px 18px -8px rgba(23,35,27,0.22); } .ds-btn-record:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #16233a; outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-btn-record-pen { width: 9px; height: 12px; background: #b4231d; clip-path: polygon(0 0, 100% 0, 100% 62%, 50% 100%, 0 62%); }

components.name: Quiet Button
components.css: .ds-btn-quiet { appearance: none; background: #f4f8f4; border: 1px solid #bcc7bb; border-radius: 2px; padding: 0.35rem 0.6rem; font-size: 0.75rem; font-weight: 600; color: #4e6152; cursor: pointer; transition: border-color 140ms ease-out, color 140ms ease-out; } .ds-btn-quiet:hover { border-color: #7c8f80; color: #17231b; } .ds-btn-quiet:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #16233a; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Select Field
components.css: .ds-field { background: #f4f8f4; color: #17231b; border: 1px solid #bcc7bb; border-radius: 2px; padding: 0.3rem 0.4rem; font-size: 0.8125rem; } .ds-field:focus-visible { border-color: #16233a; outline: none; }

components.name: Mode Tab
components.css: .ds-mode-switch { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 1fr 1fr; border: 1px solid #bcc7bb; border-radius: 2px; overflow: hidden; background: #c6cfc5; } .ds-mode { appearance: none; border: 0; background: transparent; padding: 0.4rem 0.5rem; font-size: 0.6875rem; font-weight: 700; letter-spacing: 0.1em; text-transform: uppercase; color: #4e6152; cursor: pointer; } .ds-mode[aria-selected="true"] { background: #e9f0ea; color: #17231b; box-shadow: inset 0 -2px 0 #16233a; }

components.name: Pen Row
components.description: SYS/MIC arm-state row with color swatch, name, description, and state.
components.css: .ds-pen { display: grid; grid-template-columns: auto auto 1fr auto; align-items: center; gap: 0.5rem; font-size: 0.75rem; } .ds-pen-swatch { width: 3px; height: 1.05rem; border-radius: 1px; background: #b4231d; } .ds-pen-name { font-family: ui-monospace, monospace; font-weight: 700; letter-spacing: 0.08em; color: #17231b; } .ds-pen-desc { color: #4e6152; font-size: 0.6875rem; } .ds-pen-state { font-size: 0.625rem; font-weight: 700; letter-spacing: 0.08em; text-transform: uppercase; color: #4e6152; }

components.name: Trace Line
components.description: A single transcript entry positioned on the time axis, colored per source pen.
components.html: • 00:42MICso the next step would be...
components.css: .ds-trace { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 5.25rem 1fr; gap: 0 0.85rem; align-items: baseline; list-style: none; } .ds-trace-time { font-family: ui-monospace, monospace; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; font-size: 0.6875rem; color: #4e6152; text-align: right; } .ds-trace-body { position: relative; padding-left: 0.75rem; border-left: 1px solid #bcc7bb; } .ds-trace-mic .ds-trace-body::before { content: ''; position: absolute; left: -1px; top: 0.55em; width: 7px; height: 2px; background: #b4231d; } .ds-trace-mic .ds-trace-source { font-family: ui-monospace, monospace; font-size: 0.625rem; font-weight: 700; letter-spacing: 0.1em; color: #b4231d; margin-right: 0.5rem; } .ds-trace-mic .ds-trace-text { color: #b4231d; max-width: 68ch; }

components.name: Note
components.css: .ds-note { background: #16233a; color: #e9f0ea; padding: 0.6rem 0.8rem; border-radius: 2px; font-size: 0.8125rem; line-height: 1.45; cursor: pointer; box-shadow: 0 10px 24px -12px rgba(23,35,27,0.22); }

components.name: Drop Zone
components.css: .ds-drop-zone { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 0.2rem; align-items: center; justify-content: center; padding: 1.5rem 1rem; background: #f4f8f4; border: 1px dashed #bcc7bb; border-radius: 2px; cursor: pointer; color: #4e6152; text-align: center; transition: border-color 140ms ease-out, color 140ms ease-out; } .ds-drop-zone:hover { border-color: #7c8f80; color: #17231b; } .ds-drop-line { font-weight: 600; font-size: 0.8125rem; } .ds-drop-sub { font-size: 0.6875rem; color: #4e6152; }

narrative.overview: Transcriber reads as an instrument, not an app: a paper chart mounted on a physical body, two ink pens marking a calibrated time axis, a gridded roll advancing underneath. The window is minimized during the meeting it records -- nobody watches text arrive line by line -- so the entire visual system is built for the moment after: glancing back at a chart and reading what happened, including the silences, at their true scale. This replaced an earlier verbatim-transcript direction (courtroom-stenographer paper, a single stamp-red accent) that spent its hero moment on a screen no one is looking at during capture. The chart-recorder world keeps the instinct toward a calm, non-chat metaphor but relocates the drama: two pens (SYS and MIC), each with its own ink color, draw directly onto ruled stock, and a pen-lift state exists specifically so a stalled engine is never visually indistinguishable from a quiet room -- a real bug class the old chat-log metaphor could not represent. The ruling lives in the time gutter, not across the reading column, so the chart's calibration is always visible without ever competing with the transcript text for the same pixels -- a rule this build states directly in its own CSS.
keyCharacteristics: Two pen inks, not one accent: navy SYS and red MIC, distinguished by hue because they are simultaneous, independent traces on one axis, not competing meanings.
Silence is legible, not hidden: chart speed rescales the time axis continuously so a session's true rhythm (dense stretches, six-minute silences) survives being glanced at.
The instrument's own state (pen up / pen down / pen lifted mid-run) is drawn as a visibly distinct pen position and color, never a text badge layered on top.
Grid confined to the gutter: the ruled scale never crosses into the reading column.
No waveform, no chat bubbles: the transcribed text itself is the trace.

rules.name: The Gutter-Only Grid Rule
rules.body: The ruled scale lives exclusively in the time gutter. A grid printed across the reading column is true to physical chart paper but hostile to the moment this app exists for -- reading the transcript afterward -- so the calibration and the prose never share pixels.

rules.name: The Two-Pen Rule
rules.body: SYS and MIC each own one ink color, used consistently for their swatch, trace text, and pen mark. No third pen color is introduced for any other state; the pen-lift fault state reuses MIC's red rather than adding a color, because a lifted pen is drawn as a state of the mechanism, not a new signal.

rules.name: The No Display Face Rule
rules.body: Nothing on this screen is large, bold display type. The wordmark is small and quiet; the trace text is the only content ever meant to hold attention.

rules.name: The Diffuse-Only Rule
rules.body: Every authored shadow is soft-blurred with a real offset; a hard zero-blur shadow never appears here -- it belongs to a different, neobrutalist world.

dos: Do keep the two pen inks (pen-sys navy, pen-mic red) exclusive to their own source -- trace text, swatches, and marks always match their pen.
Do confine ruled grid lines to the time gutter; never print a grid across the text-reading column.
Do represent instrument state (idle / listening / advancing / pen-lift) as a change to the pen mark itself (color + position), never as a text badge stacked on top of unchanged chrome.
Do use the diffuse ambient shadow family for anything that needs to read as lifted off the instrument; never a hard offset shadow.
donts: Don't add a third accent color; every new state maps onto SYS, MIC, or a neutral ink step.
Don't reintroduce a chat-log or chat-bubble treatment for speaker turns -- the direction explicitly refuses that pattern.
Don't bundle or fetch a display/condensed webfont for labels; the system-sans + uppercase + tracking treatment is the resolved substitute, not a placeholder.

Don't drive any meter or pen position from audio amplitude -- the event contract carries no audio levels; pen motion is chunk-arrival cadence only, and a true level meter is a named future backend cost, not something to fake visually.
